title: Economy dial: one control from frugal to strong
summary: Operator brief of 17 November 2026: one control that steers cost and usage by selecting model and reasoning level per task kind from the Token Economy ladder; usage follows from the position, no weekly budget target; medium as standard, high for hard cards, xhigh deliberately, reviews on Opus 5.5 low for now. Current state at 2adbb4f5d: nine controls, most applied at card creation (the recommendation is stamped onto unpinned cards and usually decides at launch), Claude tiers still mapped to Sonnet 5 and Haiku 4.5, economy mode a one-step boolean, cost per accepted card review-scoped, no Codex credits probe. Proposal: five positions (Frugal, Lean, Balanced, Thorough, Strong), provider-neutral rungs owned by Token Economy, matrix per task kind with floors, claim-time resolution inside model selection, same-rung quota fallback, provider preference following headroom, CLI Management surface with expected cost per accepted card and weekly percent per provider, controlled measurement of Claude weights, migration of the scattered controls. Decisions D1 to D12; slices ED-1 to ED-8.

# Economy dial policy: rung ladder, positions, matrix, floors and position store

Source: docs/economy-dial/index.html (AGT-3951) and its workbench.json. Read that Dossier first, then AGENTS.md, docs/start/contribution-and-style-guide.html, docs/system/domains/model-routing-policy.md and docs/model-selection-and-fallback/index.html. Use the Dossier's recommended option for each named decision unless a recorded operator decision selects another, and record in results/status.md which option you implemented.

Decisions: D1, D2, D5, D3 (task kind list). Dependencies: none.

Entry points: backend/Policies/model-routing-policy.v1.json, backend/Features/Pipeline/ModelRoutingPolicyRegistry.cs, backend/Features/Pipeline/ModelRoutingPolicyStateStore.cs, backend/Features/Cli/Selection/ModelSelectionPolicyStore.cs, the Token Economy package seam used for prices and ModelEquivalenceCatalog, backend/Features/Security/Iam/RoutePermissionCatalog.cs.

## Deliver
Add a versioned economy dial policy: five rungs (`light`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`) with one concrete model and thinking level per provider as in the Dossier's ladder table (Claude Haiku 5.5 medium, Opus 5.5 low/medium/high/xhigh; Codex gpt-6-luna medium, gpt-6.1-sol low/medium/high/xhigh). Read the ladder from the Token Economy package when it provides the economy dial ladder; until then use a versioned Studio mirror file and report which source is active. Define the five positions (Frugal, Lean, Balanced, Thorough, Strong; default Balanced), the task kinds and the position-by-kind matrix with floors exactly as in the Dossier's matrix table. Store the workspace position and an optional per-project position. Expose `GET /api/model-selection/dial` (policy, ladder source and version, workspace position, project positions) and `PUT /api/model-selection/dial` and `PUT /api/projects/{name}/model-selection-dial` guarded by `workspace.settings.write` and the project settings permission. Every change writes a `dial-moved` event (actor from X-Client-Id, from, to, optional note, UTC time) to the selection ledger and a history list readable through the API. Unoffered levels map with the existing highest-offered-rung rule.

## Out of scope
Using the dial in route selection (ED-3), task kind derivation (ED-2), any UI (ED-6), migration of existing controls (ED-8).

## Acceptance
- The policy reproduces the Dossier matrix; a golden test covers every position and task kind, including floors.
- Balanced resolves normal cards to medium, hard cards to high, critical to xhigh and review to Opus 5.5 low.

# Resolve the economy dial at claim time inside model selection

Source: docs/economy-dial/index.html (AGT-3951) and its workbench.json. Read that Dossier first, then AGENTS.md, docs/start/contribution-and-style-guide.html, docs/system/domains/model-routing-policy.md and docs/model-selection-and-fallback/index.html. Decisions: D3, D4 option pin-wins-visible, D5 option never, D8 option sticky-escalate, D6 same-rung fallback part. Dependencies: ED-1, ED-2.

Entry points: backend/Features/Cli/Selection/ModelSelectionService.cs, contracts ModelSelectionPlanner.cs, backend/Features/Runner/ProjectRunner.cs (about line 2776 to 2958, runModel resolution at 2957), backend/Features/Tasks/LeaseEndpoints.cs (remote claims), MechanicalFreshRunRoutePolicy, backend/Features/Cli/Quota/CliQuotaFallbackService.cs, ModelEquivalenceCatalog.cs, backend/Features/Tasks/TaskCrudEndpoints.cs (creation stamping at 1141 to 1172), ReviewDecisionOrchestrator.cs, OrchestratorSettingsResolver.cs.

## Deliver
Add the dial as a selection rule `dial` in the order of the Dossier's Figure 2: explicit card pin, then expert override (project, pipeline type, step, orchestrator), then dial (position for the card's project, task kind from ED-2, rung from the matrix), then floor, then provider and ladder, then quota admission. Cards with `modelExplicit=false` are resolved at every fresh claim, locally and through remote leases; the stamped creation recommendation no longer decides. Stop stamping a model onto unpinned cards at creation; the create preview shows the dial result instead. A same-session resume and a running process keep their route. Quota fallback for a dial-resolved route uses the same rung on the other provider; if that is capped or not accepted by the host, the run waits with a reason. Follow-up and fix rounds keep the card's current route; after a semantic failure the next fresh attempt goes one rung up, and after two failures at the stronger rung escalation stops. Extend `GET /api/model-selection/effective` with rule `dial`, rung, task kind and position. A pin below the task kind floor is honoured only as a hard pin and is flagged.

## Out of scope
Automatic provider choice (ED-4 owns the preference; use the workspace's current primary provider until then), cost projection, UI, migration of existing settings.

## Acceptance
- Moving the dial changes the route of a waiting unpinned card at its next claim without rewriting the card; tests cover local and remote claims.
- Explicit pins, hard pins, expert overrides and floors keep precedence as specified; golden tests over positions, kinds, pins and caps.
- A capped provider yields the same rung on the other provider or a wait with reason, recorded in the selection ledger.
- Reissue escalation and its stop after two failures are covered by tests.
